name: Milan Cathedral
_about: THE DUOMO OF MILAN: 158m long, the front 68m and 56.5m high, the transept 93m across, the spire 108.5m. Five aisles west of the crossing stepping down in three levels, every bay rib-vaulted, three east of it round a five-faced apse (the sacristies where the outer aisles would be); a transept with aisles of its own; two tiers of flying buttresses on every bay line, and no one kind of pinnacle (`pinnacle` parts, by turns); openwork cresting over every bay; the front a bay at a time -- portal, square window, pointed window, each under its own head -- and a broken gable, between six buttresses that set back twice, the pairs carrying three different pinnacles, the middle pair doubled; the tiburio, its four guglie, its spire and the Madonnina. Spiral turrets in the westernmost bays climb to the outer aisles' flat terraces, a stair from there to the inner ones: the aisle roofs are walked on, under the flyers.

params._innerX: the inner aisles' outer edge: the arcade between the two aisles on each side stands there
params._crossZ: the crossing's middle, four bays from the apse: the choir's two, the transept's east aisle, half the crossing

nave vaults._about: the nave's vault, bay by bay, but for the crossing's two

sacristy ends._about: the sacristies' east ends: the outer aisles stop with the choir, the apse is the inner aisles' only

outer vaults._about: the outer aisles' vaults, all but the transept's bays and the westernmost: that one is the stair turret's, under a flat terrace

inner aisle terraces._about: the inner aisles' roofs: flat, level with the inner arcade's head, against the clerestory

outer aisle terraces._about: the outer aisles' roofs, level with the outer wall's head (the west bay is the turret's terrace)

outer parapets._about: along the outer wall's head, the terrace's edge over the street

terrace stair right._about: up from the outer terrace to the inner: two flights turning on a landing

roof stair right 1._about: up from the inner terrace to the nave roof: three pairs of flights against the clerestory

arcade parapets 1._about: along the inner arcade's head, over the drop to the outer terrace: open where the stair arrives

flank buttresses._about: the lower tier: a pier against the outer wall, its flyer over the outer terrace to the inner arcade

flank pinnacles 1._about: on the lower piers, by turns: octagonal with its statue; square with four spirelets

clerestory flyers._about: the upper flyers: their piers on the inner arcade, over the inner terrace to the clerestory

outer cresting._about: the outer walls' lace, bay by bay between the buttresses

front nave._about: the bay's wall: portal, square window, pointed window

gable nave._about: the broken gable: over the nave's bay to 56.5m, and over each aisle's a rake of its own, a step down at each buttress

front buttress 1 stage 1._about: the front's buttresses: by the nave, between the aisles, at the corners, each setting back twice

front pinnacles nave._about: by the nave: the tallest, on the highest heads, DOUBLED -- two octagonal spires side by side on one head, a statue on each point

front pinnacles middle._about: between the aisles: one, octagonal, ringed by four spirelets, a statue on the point

front pinnacles corner._about: at the corners, THREE: a heavy octagonal one at the head's front...

front pinnacles corner back._about: ...and two lighter ones side by side behind it

front statues._about: a statue on a corbel, on each stage of each front buttress

transept walls right._about: the arm's two side walls (on the bay lines: a wall's thickness is behind its line), an arch through each for each aisle

transept vaults._about: four bays down each arm, their crowns the nave's

arm aisle walls._about: the arm's aisles' long walls, on the bay lines beyond them

arm aisle terraces._about: over an arm's aisle, at the outer terrace's height

arm flyers._about: over each arm's aisle from a pier on its long wall to the arm's side wall, where the arm's vault pushes out

chevet._about: the apse's walls and great windows (their heads, 24m, under the ambulatory's vault, which springs at the aisles' 25.7m)

apse flyers._about: a buttress on each corner of the apse, its flyer over the ambulatory's roof to the choir

choir arcade._about: the choir's piers and their arches into the ambulatory: the nave arcade's springing and pointed head

choir._about: the choir's clerestory, over its arcade

inner ambulatory vault._about: the inner aisles' vault carried round: their springing, rise and top

choir diaphragm._about: the wall over the choir's arch, from the nave vault's springing to the roof: the nave's last cell ends against it

ambulatory roof._about: the lean-to round the choir: a half cone cut off at the choir's wall (`oculus`) and left open there

crossing diaphragms._about: the walls over the crossing's two end arches, on which the tiburio's end faces stand

crossing squinch 1._about: the squinches: a triangle across each of the crossing's corners, carrying the tiburio's diagonal faces

crossing dome._about: the crossing's own dome inside the tiburio, struck from the octagon's foot

tiburio._about: the tiburio: the octagon over the crossing with a gable on each face, and the gallery storey on it

tiburio gallery floor._about: closing the gallery's head: the spire stands on it

tiburio spire._about: the great spire, the sky through it

tiburio spire core._about: the core in the spire's middle, with the stair up it

madonnina._about: the Madonnina, 4.16m of gilded copper, on the spire's point

guglie._about: the four guglie, on the crossing's corners

guglie flyers._about: from each guglia in to the octagon's diagonal face

stair terrace right 1._about: the flat roof over the turret's bay, round the turret's head

turret head right._about: the stair turret's head over the terrace, the spiral arriving inside it

turret head right interior._about: inside the turret's head, where the spiral arrives

stair terrace left 1._about: the flat roof over the turret's bay, round the turret's head

body interior._about: the nave and its four aisles from the facade's middle to the apse, up to the outer aisles' terraces; over the nave and the inner aisles, two more boxes stepping up as their roofs do

inner ambulatory interior._about: round the apse: the ambulatory's half ring up to the roof's foot, the choir's to the nave's

organ._about: the organ in two cases, against the north transept arm's end wall either side of its portal (Milan has no west gallery: its organs face each other across the choir)
